disposition_reason: Reports measured Pb, Cd, As and Hg (lowest, highest, average) in 27 raw chestnut honey samples from Yalova beekeepers.
disposition_locator: Tablo 2 (Heavy Metal Levels of Honey Samples, µg/kg), p.84

study.material_scope: raw chestnut honey; 8 of 27 were crystallized (all 27 analysed for metals)
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Produced and collected at 7 bee-yard spots of Yalova Beekeepers Association members, Yalova province, Turkey; not purchased at retail.
study.collection_period: 2014 ('27 chestnut honey samples obtained in 2014', p.83)
study.method: 0.5 g honey + 10 mL 65% HNO3 + 1 mL 30% H2O2, microwave digestion (Berghof MWS-3+), ICP-OES (Perkin Elmer Optima 2100DV) per Methods; Results text says ICP-MS (internal inconsistency)
study.basis: Not stated; assumed as-is honey weight (µg/kg honey).
study.qa: Only 'measurement uncertainty' (±0.004 Pb, ±0.001 Cd, ±0.001 As, ±0.003 Hg µg/kg) reported; no CRM or recovery. Analysis at Food Research laboratory of Turkish Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry.

findings.censoring: No LOD reported; source does not say how (or whether) non-detects occurred or were treated.

controls.control: Dietary risk screen: THQ and %PTDI for 3.3 g/day honey intake by a 70 kg adult
controls.outcome: THQ Pb 2.5e-4, Cd 5.56e-5, As 8.1e-5, Hg 6.45e-4; %PTDI Pb 4.4, Cd 15.4, As 4.71, Hg 4.4 (text says Hg 4.3)
controls.locator: Tablo 2 rows THQ/PTDI; Results p.85; Discussion p.87

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Summary says residues were 'below Turkish Food Codex limits' (as in the abstract), but the primary Discussion (p.87) states there is no designated maximum limit for heavy metals in honey in the Turkish Food Codex (TGK-29.12.2011). The primary is internally contradictory; summary does not flag it.
Summary omits the stated collection year (2014).
Summary states ICP-OES; primary Methods say ICP-OES but Results text says ICP-MS (unflagged inconsistency).
Summary does not note the Discussion's reference to '30 chestnut honey samples' for Hg versus n=27 elsewhere.
Summary table reproduces PTDI Hg 4.4% from Tablo 2 without noting text gives 4.3%, and THQ Cd 5.56e-5 vs text 5.5e-5.
unresolved: Instrument conflict: ICP-OES (Methods, Tablo 1) vs ICP-MS (Results p.85).
n for Hg: 27 (Methods) vs '30 chestnut honey samples' (Discussion p.87).
Cd distribution implausible: mean 1.183 µg/kg vs max 1.198 and min 0.076 µg/kg; cannot be verified without per-sample data.
No LOD/LOQ; values as low as 0.032 µg/kg As by ICP-OES are well below typical ICP-OES capability; reliability of low-end values unverified.
Sampling spot names and per-spot results not reported.
